provenance.note: Two of the three units live in the reference's integration utilities, so `multisig-utils.ts` is **transpiled in memory** by the reference's own pinned TypeScript and evaluated with a module shim, as the `client-multisig-inception` generator does. The third, `multisigRevoke`, is written inline in a test body and is driven through the reference's own `revoke` and `send` in the same order. Nothing is written into the submodule. The clock and the agent's key are pinned; the local member is the reference's own `mockGetAID`. `PUBLIC TEST MATERIAL`: the passcode and sealed salt are the pinned tests' own.

declarations.create_registry_multisig: export async function createRegistryMultisig( client: SignifyClient, aid: HabState, otherMembersAIDs: HabState[], multisigAID: HabState, registryName: string, nonce: string, isInitiator: boolean = false ) { if (!isInitiator) await waitAndMarkNotification(client, '/multisig/vcp'); const vcpResult = await client.registries().create({ name: multisigAID.name, registryName: registryName, nonce: nonce, }); const op = await vcpResult.op(); const serder = vcpResult.regser; const anc = vcpResult.serder; const sigs = vcpResult.sigs; const sigers = sigs.map((sig) => new signify.Siger({ qb64: sig })); const ims = signify.d(signify.messagize(anc, sigers)); const atc = ims.substring(anc.size); const regbeds = { vcp: [serder, ''], anc: [anc, atc], }; const recp = otherMembersAIDs.map((aid) => aid.prefix); await client .exchanges() .send( aid.name, 'registry', aid, '/multisig/vcp', { gid: multisigAID.prefix }, regbeds, recp ); return op; }
declarations.issue_credential_multisig: export async function issueCredentialMultisig( client: SignifyClient, aid: HabState, otherMembersAIDs: HabState[], multisigAIDName: string, kargsIss: CredentialData, isInitiator: boolean = false ) { if (!isInitiator) await waitAndMarkNotification(client, '/multisig/iss'); const credResult = await client .credentials() .issue(multisigAIDName, kargsIss); const op = credResult.op; const multisigAID = await client.identifiers().get(multisigAIDName); const keeper = client.manager!.get(multisigAID); const sigs = await keeper.sign(signify.b(credResult.anc.raw)); const sigers = sigs.map((sig: string) => new signify.Siger({ qb64: sig })); const ims = signify.d(signify.messagize(credResult.anc, sigers)); const atc = ims.substring(credResult.anc.size); const embeds = { acdc: [credResult.acdc, ''], iss: [credResult.iss, ''], anc: [credResult.anc, atc], }; const recp = otherMembersAIDs.map((aid) => aid.prefix); await client .exchanges() .send( aid.name, 'multisig', aid, '/multisig/iss', { gid: multisigAID.prefix }, embeds, recp ); return op; }
declarations.multisig_revoke: async function multisigRevoke( client: SignifyClient, memberName: string, groupName: string, rev: Serder, anc: Serder ) { const leaderHab = await client.identifiers().get(memberName); const groupHab = await client.identifiers().get(groupName); const members = await client.identifiers().members(groupName); const keeper = client.manager!.get(groupHab); const sigs = await keeper.sign(b(anc.raw)); const sigers = sigs.map((sig: string) => new Siger({ qb64: sig })); const ims = d(messagize(anc, sigers)); const atc = ims.substring(anc.size); const embeds = { iss: [rev, ''], anc: [anc, atc], }; const recipients = members.signing .map((m: { aid: string }) => m.aid) .filter((aid: string) => aid !== leaderHab.prefix); await client .exchanges() .send( memberName, 'multisig', leaderHab, '/multisig/rev', { gid: groupHab.prefix }, embeds, recipients ); }

notes.discarding: `await waitAndMarkNotification(client, route);` as a statement — the SAID is never bound
notes.slots: an issuance embeds `{acdc, iss, anc}` and a revocation embeds `{iss, anc}`, so the two share a slot name

pinned_confirmations.note: a registry proposal embeds `{vcp, anc}` and an issuance embeds `{acdc, iss, anc}`; only the anchor carries an attachment, because its signature is what authorizes the rest.

a_joining_member_never_reads_the_proposa.note: both helpers wait for a bell and discard the SAID it carries. No `getRequest` is ever made — driven here across six calls, none of which fetches a group request — so a joining member builds from its own arguments and nothing compares the result with what was proposed.
a_joining_member_never_reads_the_proposa.rust_decision: the proposal is read and the value that decides the identifier is taken from it: `accept_registry` uses the nonce out of the proposed inception and `accept_issuance` compares the credential SAID it derived with the one it was shown. A mismatch is a typed error.

a_different_nonce_is_a_different_registr.declaration: `createRegistryMultisig(..., nonce, ...)` — the nonce is the caller's, on both halves
a_different_nonce_is_a_different_registr.note: a registry identifier is a digest over its inception and the nonce is inside it. Two members handed the same nonce derive the same registry; handed different ones they derive different registries and neither call fails. The group then holds two registries and agrees on none.
a_different_nonce_is_a_different_registr.rust_decision: the nonce is required on the proposing half — the endpoint beneath draws one from the operating system when it is absent, which for a group means every member deriving a different registry — and read from the proposal on the joining half.

different_attributes_are_a_different_cre.declaration: `issueCredentialMultisig(..., kargsIss, ...)` — the credential data is the caller's, on both halves
different_attributes_are_a_different_cre.note: the same shape as the registry: every field of a credential is inside its SAID, so two members handed different attributes issue different credentials with no error on either side.
different_attributes_are_a_different_cre.rust_decision: the credential SAID this member derives is compared with the one the proposal carries.

a_revocation_travels_in_the_issuance_slo.note: the route says revocation and the embed carries the revocation event under the issuance label. A reader narrowing through the reference's own `assertMultisigRev` — which declares `e: { rev, d? }` — finds no `rev` at all. The `client-multisig-events` route-and-embed scan turned this up and left it here.
a_revocation_travels_in_the_issuance_slo.rust_decision: the revocation travels in `rev`, which is the slot the exchange route table names for this route and the one the KERIA API schema declares. The reference's own pairing does not classify here.

the_issuance_result_drops_its_signatures.note: `issue` computes the anchor's signatures and posts them, then returns `{ acdc, anc, iss, op }` without them — so `issueCredentialMultisig` fetches the group identifier again, rebuilds its keeper, and signs the same bytes a second time just to build the attachment. `revoke` returns `{ anc, rev, op }` and has the same gap.
the_issuance_result_drops_its_signatures.rust_decision: `IssuanceArtifacts.anchor` is an `IdentifierArtifact` — the event with its signatures — so the attachment is built from what the endpoint already returned and nothing is signed twice.

one_round_is_filed_under_a_different_top.note: a registry proposal is sent under the topic `registry` where every other multisig round uses `multisig` — and the pinned tree is not even consistent with itself: of its three `/multisig/vcp` sends, two use `registry` and one uses `multisig`. A member filtering notifications by topic therefore sees registry proposals in two places.
one_round_is_filed_under_a_different_top.rust_decision: the majority form is reproduced — the exchanges endpoint's own `REGISTRY_TOPIC` for this one route — because it is what `createRegistryMultisig`, the ported unit, sends. The disagreement is recorded rather than resolved, since nothing in the pinned tree settles which is intended.
